question: How does BSP actually buy companies?
html:
How BSP buys

BSP buys theme-first. It studies a sector in advance, then buys an anchor company in a banked process from either an exiting sponsor or a founder, and builds through add-ons. These patterns are inferred from public evidence, not BSP's internal screening criteria (BSP acquisition methodology).

Thesis before target

  • Deal releases present each company as the result of prior sector work. RJ David spent "over a year" in electrical services before CET, and Adam Glucksman tracked accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are non-discretionary. Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer bet (BSP acquisition methodology).

Two seller types

Seller typeDealsTypical pattern
Sponsor secondary (larger checks)Thomas Scientific (Carlyle, Jan 27, 2022); BPI (Svoboda, Apr 27, 2023); Frontline (BV, Dec 11, 2024)Outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority. The inherited CEO is replaced at about 13-15 months (Simmons to Haas; Naidoo to Britt)
Founder or partner owner (smaller checks)Fair Harbor (Mar 23, 2022); Smith + Howard (Nov 15, 2022); Punctual Pros (Apr 3, 2024); CET (Feb 2025)First institutional capital. Founder CEOs stay (Taylor, Buckwalter, Duquette)

(BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile)

Banked, adviser-heavy processes

  • Six of seven anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists" (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).

Capital structure varies

  • Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche at LIBOR+625. A PIK amendment followed in Q4 2024, and the loan was later marked at about 88% of par (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Fair Harbor shows equity only on the public record (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • Smith + Howard used an alternative practice structure, with BSP investing in the advisory entity rather than the CPA firm (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • The main fund reports $335M sold. A separate Frontline vehicle raised $136.95M in Dec 2024. The $50-250M check range is unverified (BSP firm profile). Against $0.9-2.1B rival flagships, BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (Private-equity landscape).

Add-ons and gaps

  • BSP states 23 add-ons. 21 are identified by name. Frontline and Fair Harbor have none (BSP acquisition methodology).
  • The add-on sequencing detail is cut off in the context. Add-on timing, pricing and sourcing need the full add-on list.

Next actions

  • Pull the full add-on list and confirm the two unidentified add-ons (one at Punctual Pros, one at Smith + Howard).
  • Test the CEO-transition pattern at BPI, where Andrew Bleeker is still CEO, against the 13-15 month norm (est.).
  • For Punctual Pros, prioritise proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA instead of auctions, where Sila, Gridiron and Watchtower set the pricing (Private-equity landscape).
  • Map Frontline's law-firm IT and billing add-on targets before a generalist IT services consolidator builds a legal vertical (Private-equity landscape).

# How BSP buys

BSP buys theme-first. It studies a sector in advance, then buys an anchor company in a banked process from either an exiting sponsor or a founder, and builds through add-ons. These patterns are inferred from public evidence, not BSP's internal screening criteria (BSP acquisition methodology).

## Thesis before target

- Deal releases present each company as the result of prior sector work. RJ David spent "over a year" in electrical services before CET, and Adam Glucksman tracked accounting before Smith + Howard (BSP acquisition methodology).
- Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are non-discretionary. Fair Harbor is the only discretionary consumer bet (BSP acquisition methodology).

## Two seller types

| Seller type | Deals | Typical pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Sponsor secondary (larger checks) | Thomas Scientific (Carlyle, Jan 27, 2022); BPI (Svoboda, Apr 27, 2023); Frontline (BV, Dec 11, 2024) | Outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority. The inherited CEO is replaced at about 13-15 months (Simmons to Haas; Naidoo to Britt) |
| Founder or partner owner (smaller checks) | Fair Harbor (Mar 23, 2022); Smith + Howard (Nov 15, 2022); Punctual Pros (Apr 3, 2024); CET (Feb 2025) | First institutional capital. Founder CEOs stay (Taylor, Buckwalter, Duquette) |

(BSP acquisition methodology; BSP firm profile)

## Banked, adviser-heavy processes

- Six of seven anchor deals had a named sell-side adviser. Punctual Pros went to "eight finalists" (BSP acquisition methodology).
- Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET. Harris Williams advised on Punctual Pros and Frontline. Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal (BSP acquisition methodology).

## Capital structure varies

- Thomas used an Apollo/MidCap unitranche at LIBOR+625. A PIK amendment followed in Q4 2024, and the loan was later marked at about 88% of par (BSP acquisition methodology).
- Fair Harbor shows equity only on the public record (BSP acquisition methodology).
- Smith + Howard used an alternative practice structure, with BSP investing in the advisory entity rather than the CPA firm (BSP acquisition methodology).
- The main fund reports $335M sold. A separate Frontline vehicle raised $136.95M in Dec 2024. The $50-250M check range is unverified (BSP firm profile). Against $0.9-2.1B rival flagships, BSP leans on co-invest and operating credibility (Private-equity landscape).

## Add-ons and gaps

- BSP states 23 add-ons. 21 are identified by name. Frontline and Fair Harbor have none (BSP acquisition methodology).
- The add-on sequencing detail is cut off in the context. Add-on timing, pricing and sourcing need the full add-on list.

## Next actions

- Pull the full add-on list and confirm the two unidentified add-ons (one at Punctual Pros, one at Smith + Howard).
- Test the CEO-transition pattern at BPI, where Andrew Bleeker is still CEO, against the 13-15 month norm (est.).
- For Punctual Pros, prioritise proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA instead of auctions, where Sila, Gridiron and Watchtower set the pricing (Private-equity landscape).
- Map Frontline's law-firm IT and billing add-on targets before a generalist IT services consolidator builds a legal vertical (Private-equity landscape).
